meta.title: The Number on the Stone
meta.textType: story: a club trip to the old town, with a history sign

paragraphs: On Saturday, February thirteenth, the Explorers took the bus to the old town with Teacher Kim. At nine o'clock, they stood in front of the old gate. A brick arch stood over the path, and a carved stone sat above it. A sign beside the gate said, "This gate was built more than two hundred years ago. It was closed every night." "Two centuries is a long time," said Teacher Kim. "It is only old stones," said Leo. "A king does not even live here." A thin spider's web covered the carved stone, and small drops of dew hung on it. Lily looked up and said, "The web hides the number." Mia zoomed in with her camera and took a photo of the stone. The number on her screen was too small to read.

The gallery was close to the old well. At ten o'clock, the Explorers climbed its wooden stairs. Leo was the first one on the stairs. Old black-and-white photos of the past hung on the walls. "I like the gallery better than the gate," said Leo. "Photos are more fun than stones." Mia stopped in front of one photo and read the card under it. The card said, "The Old Gate, eighteen sixty. The gate is forty years old." The photo was taken from the path, and it showed the same arch. Mia looked at it for a long time. Then she wrote a number in her notebook and said nothing. "What did you write?" asked Leo. Mia only smiled.

At half past ten, the Explorers sat on a bench next to the stone wall. Mia opened the photo album on her camera. It had two photos of the gate and one photo of the old well. She chose the photo of the stone and made it bigger with two fingers. "Look at the stone: eighteen twenty!" she said. The number was clear on the screen. Lily leaned over Mia's shoulder and read it again. Leo stood behind them and looked at the screen for a long time. He did not say one word about old stones.

Teacher Kim came to the bench and looked at the screen. "The web hid the number, but somebody found it," she said. "Sightseeing is more fun when you look closely." "Who worked it out?" May sat next to Mia and saw the page of Mia's notebook. "She did," said May. "I did only a small sum," said Mia. She smiled and looked at her shoes.

At eleven o'clock, the children went to the tea shop. It was crowded, so they waited a long time for their juice. Leo held Mia's camera and looked at the stone one more time. "Maybe old stones can talk," he said. "Only if you count," said Mia.
text.summary: On the old town walk, a spider's web hides the number on the stone above the old gate. Mia says nothing, but she works out the year, and later she shows it on her camera.
